newsitem.title: UK: Major calls for UK debate on EU, no referendum yet.
newsitem.headline: Major calls for UK debate on EU, no referendum yet.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Tuesday that there should be a "rational debate" on all aspects of the European Union but he rejected calls for a referendum on Britain's membership of the EU or, for the moment, on whether it should ever adopt a single European currency.

Major was responding in parliament to anti-European lawmaker Teresa Gorman who brought to his attention a newspaper poll showing 68 percent of Britons were opposed to economic and monetary union (EMU) and almost half did not want to be in the EU at all. She said a referendum should be held "to clear the air".

However, Major reiterated government policy since last April which, he said, was to hold a referendum only if the government decided to take the country into the single currency, and on that specific question.

"What we need in this country is a rational debate on the issue of Europe, so that not just on the issue of a single currency, but upon all the important issues that lie ahead of us in the Inter-Governmental Conference, people have a reasoned debate and are then able to make reasoned judgments on the basis of facts and not scares," he said.
